### [3] Notion — Pricing
**Grade: INACCURATE**

**Claims from documents:**
- "Plus/$12 monthly or $10 annual" [citations.md:29]
- "Business/$24 monthly or $20 annual" [citations.md:29]
- Platform-overview.md Table shows: Plus "Monthly: $12, Annual: $10" and Business "Monthly: $24, Annual: $20" [platform-overview.md:96-101]

**Source evidence:**
```
Free: $0/member/month
Plus: $10/member/month (monthly), $12/member/month annual equivalent ($120/year)
Business: $20/member/month (monthly), $24/member/month annual equivalent ($240/year)
Enterprise: Custom pricing
```

**Assessment:** **Status: RESOLVED — FALSE POSITIVE.** The fetched temp file was
confusingly worded by the WebFetch model, but the documents are correct. The
standard SaaS pattern (annual cheaper than monthly) combined with "Save up to
20% with yearly" confirms: Plus $12/month billed monthly, $10/month billed
annually ($120/year). The temp file text "$10/member/month (monthly)" was a
garbled extraction, not a faithful representation of the source page.

**Other pricing claims VERIFIED:**
- Free tier: 5MB file upload, 7-day history, 10 guests [platform-overview.md:98] matches source
- Custom domains $8–10/month [citations.md:29, notion-vs-obsidian.md:100] matches "Custom domains: $8-10/month per domain"
- Custom Agents $10/1,000 credits [citations.md:29] matches source
- File upload limits (5MB free, ~5GB paid) [citations.md:29] matches source

**INACCURATE** due to inverted monthly/annual pricing structure.

### [10] Notion Engineering Blog — How we made Notion available offline
**Grade: VERIFIED**

**Claims from documents:**
- SQLite-based persistent storage layer [citations.md:79, offline-local-first.md:53-54]
- "forest of offline page trees" [citations.md:79, offline-local-first.md:58-69]
- Two tables: offline_page, offline_action [citations.md:79]
- Push-based sync (not polling) [citations.md:79, offline-local-first.md:74-80]
- lastDownloadedTimestamp per page [citations.md:79]
- "new CRDT data model for conflict-resolution" [citations.md:79, offline-local-first.md:86-87]

**Source evidence:**
```
Storage Layer:
Evolved SQLite caching into persistent storage layer.

Offline Trees & Tracking:
"Forest of offline page trees" handles multiple reasons a page might be offline

Two core tables:
- offline_page: One row per available offline page/database
- offline_action: Records why each page is offline (origin_page_id, from_page_id,
  impacted_page_id, type)

Sync Architecture:
Push-based update distribution (not polling):
- Each client tracks lastDownloadedTimestamp per offline page
- On reconnect, timestamps compared against server's lastUpdatedTime

Conflict Resolution:
Migration to "new CRDT data model for conflict-resolution" for rich-text handling.
```

**Assessment:** All technical implementation claims match engineering blog. VERIFIED.

### [18] Notion Developer Docs — API Upgrade Guide (2025-09-03)
**Grade: VERIFIED**

**Claims from documents:**
- Multi-source databases (single database with multiple linked data sources) [citations.md:137, automation-api.md:24]
- Breaking changes (not backwards-compatible) [citations.md:137, automation-api.md:26-29]

**Source evidence:**
```
Core Feature: Multi-Source Databases
"First-class support for multi-source databases" - single database with multiple
linked data sources.

Breaking Changes:
NOT backwards-compatible. Existing integrations fail when users add additional
data sources

Major API Restructuring:
- Database ID → Data Source ID transition
- New /v1/data_sources namespace replaces /v1/databases
- Retrieve Database endpoint returns list of child data_sources

Migration (6-Step):
1. Implement discovery to fetch/cache data_source_id values
2. Supply data_source_id for page creation and relations
3. Migrate database endpoints to data source equivalents
4. Update Search API result handling
5. Upgrade TypeScript SDK to v5.0.0+
6. Modify webhook subscriptions for new event types

Webhook Changes:
New events: data_source.content_updated, schema_updated, created, moved, deleted,
undeleted
```

**Assessment:** All API upgrade claims match source documentation exactly. VERIFIED.

The pricing.md source DOES mention "Business+: Conditional logic in forms; advanced automations" but doesn't explicitly map "database automations" to specific tiers.
